design.research_question: S13: does knowing the individual improve prediction?

conditions.population: trained on other dyads' deceiver rows (target's whole dyad excluded, and sub01_sub02 excluded from the training pool entirely)
conditions.personalized: trained on target participant's first ceil(2n/3) of own deceiver trials, chronologically ordered by dyad_trial_seq

design.split: per-participant chronological, dyad_trial_seq, ceil(2n/3) train / remainder test (323/161 for every participant, since every deceiver block is 484 rows)
design.aggregation: mean of the dyad's participants' delta

inner_cv.personalized: TimeSeriesSplit(3), falls back to StratifiedKFold(3, shuffle=False) if any inner fold lacks both classes (S19 chronology)

design.relation_to_exp1_exp2: exp1 pooled LR AUROC and exp2 LODO LR AUROC are read at runtime for the cross-experiment table (Step 9); neither is used in any exp3 computation.

unit_of_analysis_resolution.aggregation: mean of the dyad's participants' per-participant delta
unit_of_analysis_resolution.prose: S13 instructs recording each participant's score individually and computing the aggregate via S20, not by pooling trials across participants. S20 and results/frozen_hypotheses.md (frozen before any model was fit) fix the unit of analysis as the dyad, n=11 for exp3. These are read as consistent, not competing: S13's 'individually' governs what is measured (forbidding trial-pooling across participants into one AUROC), not what is statistically tested. So measurement happens at participant grain (21 participants, all five metrics, both conditions); the dyad-grain delta is the arithmetic mean of the dyad's participants' deltas (the only aggregation that uses both participants when present, is symmetric in them, and reduces to the lone participant's delta for sub19_sub22); S20's sign test and paired sign-flip permutation test run on those 11 dyad-grain values. The 21-value participant-grain sign test is also reported, labelled secondary and non-independent (dyad partners share dyad/sessions/opponent and, for the population condition, the same training set).

excluded_participants.sub01: dyad sub01_sub02 excluded from exp3 by frozen_hypotheses.md (n=11 for exp3); sub01 additionally excluded from population training pool (Step 4b).
excluded_participants.sub02: no deceiver-role session was ever recorded for sub01_sub02 (archive gap); sub02 has zero deceiver rows in single_brain.parquet.
excluded_participants.sub22: the Player_sub22_Observer_sub19 session was unrecoverable in S9 EEG preprocessing (see data/processed/onednn_notes.md); sub22 has zero deceiver rows in the feature table even though the dyad survives via sub19.

participant_reconciliation.gate_did_not_see: sub19_sub22 participant-grain asymmetry (single deceiver-side participant) -- the S7 gate computed exp3's fold sizes from trial_table.csv, which still shows 968 trials for this dyad because it predates the S9 preprocessing loss.

gate_recheck.note: The frozen gate's numbers were computed at dyad grain on data/processed/trial_table.csv (smallest fold minority 70); this recheck is at participant grain on the exp3 held-out blocks and was never seen by the original gate.

per_participant_scores.held_out_block: last third of each participant's own deceiver dyad_trial_seq (323/161)

per_dyad_scores.aggregation: mean of the dyad's participants' per-participant delta

secondary_participant_grain.independence_caveat: Non-independent: participants within a dyad share the same dyad, sessions, opponent, and (population condition) the same training set. Reported for consistency (S23), not as the primary inferential test.

sensitivity_n10.note: sub19_sub22 additionally dropped (single-participant dyad); no refitting, reuses the same per-participant scores as the primary run.

cross_experiment.interpretation: Personalized mean AUROC exceeds population mean AUROC. This supports H2 (person-specific signature) descriptively; the S20 paired test at dyad grain (n=11) is the actual inferential claim, not this mean comparison.
cross_experiment.note: exp3's population number is a near-neighbour of exp2's LODO number but is not the same quantity: exp2 scores whole held-out dyads, exp3 scores only the last third of one participant's deceiver trials. Everything in this project sits within a few points of chance (exp1's headline was 0.534); a 0.53-ish number is not dressed up as a strong result. With 11 dyads, small differences are not overinterpreted (S22).

10_reproducibility.note: TimeSeriesSplit has no random_state; deterministic by construction.

gate_json_exp3_row.reason: Smallest fold minority (70) clears threshold (60); 11/11 included dyads individually clear it (needed >= 10).
gate_json_exp3_row.assumption: The spec's own example ('train rounds 1-30, test rounds 31-40') does not map onto this dataset's 'round' field, which only spans 1-11 per session (44 trials/round) -- not the 30+ rounds the example implies. Standing in for the held-out block: the late tercile of the dyad's own dyad_trial_seq (2e), i.e. train = early+middle, test = late. This is stated as an assumption, not a fact pinned down by the spec.
